title: Isolated-deploy packaging sprint: license + support + upgrade cadence experiments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a focused set of experiments to converge on a predictable commercial and operational packaging model for isolated deployments (VPC and on-prem). Deliverables: (1) license fee structure (flat + usage credit variants), (2) three support/service tiers mapped to SLAs, (3) recommended upgrade cadence and guarded upgrade playbook for air-gapped customers.
background: Enterprise customers requesting Private/VPC and on-prem options repeatedly ask for clearer pricing and upgrade guarantees. Current proposals are fragmented across legal, sales, and engineering. Prior work (entitlement pilots, reserved capacity experiments) surfaced trade-offs between predictability for finance and flexibility for engineering. This ticket consolidates a runnable experiment matrix to validate commercial and operational choices with 3 pilot customers.
goals: Reduce negotiation cycles for Private contracts by 30% within pilot cohort
Define 2 license fee primitives (subscription + capacity credits) and quantify customer cost at representative workloads
Establish a support tier mapping (Silver/Gold/Platinum) with clear SLA ladder and runbook requirements
Agree a default upgrade cadence and a hardened opt-out path for air-gapped customers
success_metrics: # of pilot customers that accept the proposed package without bespoke amendments >= 2
Average time to close (contract signature) reduced by 20% for pilots
Support ticket surge on upgrade windows <= 15% above baseline when following playbook
Observed P99 tail latency regressions <= 5% during scheduled upgrades in a canary cohort
proposal_variants: Variant A - Flat license + annual capacity credits: annual license fee scaled by node count with pre-bought GPU-hour credits that discount overcommit bursts
Variant B - Usage-forward subscription: lower fixed fee + per-token/per-embedding metered overage; includes network egress band for VPC deployments
Variant C - Hybrid reserve: monthly reserved capacity (guaranteed throughput), with per-use credits for bursts and optional premium support add-on
Support tier definitions: Silver (business hours, 24h response for Sev1), Gold (24/7, 4h Sev1), Platinum (24/7, 1h Sev1 + dedicated CSM + ops-runbook partnership)
experiment_timeline: Week 1: Align legal on permissive contract language prototypes and minimum refundable credits
Week 2: Pricing models validated with finance for unit economics; run internal margin simulations
Week 3-6: Pilot with 3 customers - two VPC, one on-prem air-gapped (staggered start); collect contract negotiation feedback
Week 7: Run upgrade cadence test with canary subset and collect telemetry (latency/cost/support volume)
Week 8: Synthesize findings, finalize term sheets and playbooks, craft sales enablement materials
stakeholders: Engineering: Miguel Ortega (runtime lead), Priya Iyer (ops)
open_questions: What minimum refundable commitment do we need to cover reserved capacity risk?
Should upgrade cadence be expressed as a fixed window (quarterly) or SLA-backed optional maintenance windows?
How to price egress/network costs for VPC deployments in multi-region setups?
Do we offer an automated rollback guarantee for Platinum customers during upgrades? If so, how to quantify cost exposure?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales pressure to carve bespoke discounts undermines standardization. Mitigation: Define a single variance allowance table and require PM/Finance sign-off for deviations.
Risk: Engineering burn from tight upgrade SLAs for air-gapped customers. Mitigation: Create an 'assisted upgrade' paid service; codify rollback/health-check automation before customer-facing window.
Risk: Security questionnaire gaps for on-prem templates. Mitigation: Pre-fill common SaaS/infra questionnaire answers and run tabletop review with Security to produce a reusable package.
Risk: Unexpected support load during first upgrades. Mitigation: Staff a cross-functional on-call rotation and require runbook dry-run before production window
